title: Email services, inbound/outbound email, and limits overview
objectives: Distinguish inbound Apex email services from outbound Messaging.sendEmail.
Cite Execution Governors and Limits: 10 sendEmail methods per transaction and 50 MB email-services heap.
Refuse invented daily mass-email allocations; point at the email section of the governors page.
Keep email sending after a successful transaction unless the product explicitly needs otherwise.
diagnostic_question: A trigger sends an email per LAB_Case__c in a 200-row insert and also exposes an inbound email service. Which governors apply, and what breaks first?
definition: Outbound Apex email uses Messaging.sendEmail (SingleEmailMessage / MassEmailMessage). Inbound Apex email services implement Messaging.InboundEmailHandler to parse messages sent to an email-service address. Per-transaction governors include 10 sendEmail method calls and a 50 MB heap for email services. Daily deliverability allocations are on the same governors topic's email section and are org/edition-sensitive—do not invent them. ([Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm); [Apex Developer Guide — email](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_email_outbound.htm))
why_it_matters: Triggers that sendEmail in a loop die at 10 calls. Inbound handlers that load huge attachments hit the 50 MB email-services heap. Interviewers also listen for 'email is not a Queueable substitute' and 'do not invent daily caps.'
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a company mailroom. Outbound is the franking machine: Messaging.sendEmail, 10 button-presses per transaction on the governors table. Inbound is the receiving chute: InboundEmailHandler on an email-service address, with a 50 MB heap. Daily postage is a different table on the same governors page—look it up, do not guess. Sending inside a transaction that later rolls back is a product decision; prefer send after commit via the save-order post-commit path or a Queueable. Never put secrets in email bodies.
deeper_explanation: Execution Governors and Limits lists total sendEmail methods allowed as 10 per transaction (sync and async). Email services heap size is 50 MB (footnote on heap). Quote only these unless you re-open the email-limits section of that same page for daily/mass numbers. ([Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

Outbound: Messaging.sendEmail with SingleEmailMessage or MassEmailMessage. Prefer setTargetObjectId / templates over raw HTML with PII. Bulkify: one sendEmail call can take a list—do not call sendEmail 200 times. ([Apex email outbound](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_email_outbound.htm))

Inbound: configure an Email Service in Setup, bind a class implementing Messaging.InboundEmailHandler.handleInboundEmail. That class is metadata; the messages are data. Attachments and large bodies consume the 50 MB email-services heap. Authenticate senders; do not auto-run DML from untrusted mail.

Limits overview means: per-transaction 10 sendEmail + 50 MB inbound heap from the governors page, plus a pointer to that page's email section for daily allocations. Deliverability, bounce handling, and Org-Wide Email Addresses are neighboring admin topics.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Inbound: Email Service plus InboundEmailHandler, 50 MB heap. Outbound: Messaging.sendEmail, 10 calls per transaction. Daily caps live on the governors email section—I will not invent them. Do not sendEmail in a 200-row loop.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I split inbound vs outbound. I bulk outbound into list sends so I stay at or under 10 method calls. I treat the handler class as metadata and inbound messages as data. I look up daily allocations on Execution Governors and Limits instead of quoting a blog. I do not use email as a platform-event bus. I consider Queueable if sending must happen after a heavy save.

when_to_use: When Apex must send mail: outbound Messaging.sendEmail with list bulkification and the 10-call cap.
When vendors mail a mailbox you control: inbound email services with InboundEmailHandler.
When quoting limits: 10 sendEmail and 50 MB email-services heap from Execution Governors and Limits.
When someone asks for daily mass-email numbers: open that governors page's email section rather than inventing.
When sending must not run on a rolled-back save: after-commit / Queueable design (APEX-010/011).
When inbound mail should create LAB_ cases with untrusted-body hygiene.
when_not_to_use: Do not sendEmail once per row in a 200-row trigger.
Do not invent daily email allocation numbers in an interview.
Do not use Apex email as a substitute for platform events (APEX-012) or HTTP callouts (APEX-013).
Do not treat inbound handlers as trusted; they are unauthenticated SMTP unless you add checks.
Do not put session IDs or named-credential secrets in templates.
Do not use production customer mailboxes for the lab.
configuration_or_code_location: Setup → Email Services; Apex class implementing InboundEmailHandler.
Setup → Org-Wide Email Addresses / Deliverability (admin neighboring).

interview_questions.question: Inbound vs outbound Apex email?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Inbound: Email Service plus InboundEmailHandler, 50 MB heap. Outbound: Messaging.sendEmail, 10 calls per transaction. Daily caps: look up.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep humans on email and systems on events/callouts. I bulk outbound lists. I treat inbound as untrusted. I cite Execution Governors and Limits rather than blogs.
weak_answer_warnings: Collapsing Email-to-Case, alerts, and sendEmail into one limit

interview_questions.question: Which email limits will you quote from the Apex Developer Guide?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: 10 sendEmail per transaction and 50 MB email-services heap. Anything daily/mass I re-open the governors email section.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Interviewers reward this humility. I also know async still has 10 sendEmail. I do not mix in 100 callouts. I mention Limits.getEmailInvocations for evidence.

interview_questions.question: Case trigger emails each contact on a 200-row insert. What fails?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: sendEmail per row can exceed 10 method calls. Build a list or chunk Queueables.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would show Limits.getEmailInvocations in a test with 20 rows expecting 1. I would not catch the governor. I would check duplicate emails and individual email preferences as neighboring.
follow_ups: How do you test without sending?

interview_questions.question: Inbound service dies on a huge attachment. First check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Email services heap is 50 MB, not the normal 6/12 MB. Reject or offload attachments.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at MIME size, debug heap, and whether the handler concatenates all parts. I do not raise CPU first. I add a test with a large Blob if practical, or document the cap.
interview_questions.example: PDF plus many images in one inbound invoice mail.
tradeoffs: Store in Files vs inline Blob
follow_ups: What about heap in Queueable after inbound?

interview_questions.question: When is Apex email the wrong integration tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When an ERP or many subscribers need structured facts—use CDC/platform events or callouts.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Email is human-scale, lossy, and hard to parse. I keep inbound handlers for mailbox use cases. I do not XML-email an ERP that can subscribe to the bus.
interview_questions.example: CDC on LAB_Order__c instead of emailing XML.
weak_answer_warnings: Building an integration bus on sendEmail

interview_questions.question: Tests pass, UAT inbox empty.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Sandbox deliverability is often off. Assert sendEmail invocations and reserved addresses, not Gmail.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check Organization-Wide defaults, deliverability set to system email only, and bounce. I do not 'fix' by SeeAllData. I use setTargetObjectId in tests carefully with synthetic contacts.
interview_questions.example: Messaging.sendEmail in test with deliverability suppressed.
follow_ups: How to send to a real tester in UAT?

interview_questions.question: Need 25 emails from one user save.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Cannot handle the governor. Chunk across Queueable/Batch transactions, each with ≤10 sendEmail calls.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I design idempotent sends (custom 'already mailed' field) so retries do not spam. I watch daily allocations on the governors email section. I consider whether a template + mass email fits better.
follow_ups: Does finish() of Batch send a summary instead?
weak_answer_warnings: try/catch around sendEmail to swallow LimitException

interview_questions.question: How do you secure an inbound email service?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Allowlist senders, treat body as untrusted, least-privilege handler, no secrets in replies, synthetic LAB_ data in tests.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Email services can create records as the running context of the service—I check the Setup user and sharing (APEX-015). I do not expose a public address that runs unrestricted DML. I log message-ids not bodies with PII.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CaseInbound ignores senders not in LAB_AllowedSender__mdt.
follow_ups: What user does the service run as?
